newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM CONFIDENT FOCUS 2000 CAN MEET TARGET.
newsitem.headline: KLM CONFIDENT FOCUS 2000 CAN MEET TARGET.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday its Focus 2000 restructuring programme was on target to increase operating income by 1.5 billion guilders over the next three years.
"The assessments so far confirm the possibility to structurally improve operating income by 1.5 billion guilders over a three-year period," KLM said.

The airline earlier reported third-quarter operating results dwindled to a 19 million guilder loss from a year-earlier 56 million guilder profit, undermined by spiralling fuel costs, a hefty wage bill and increased third party and landing charges.
KLM said the Focus 2000 programme, announced in November at the presentation of its half-year results, had identified major improvement projects.
"Most projects are defined, project managers appointed and financial goals set," it said.
Unions and works councils would need to be consulted on new projects, it added.
Projects already being implemented included the development of a new revenue management system, electronic shopping and the introduction of a new sales and distribution approach.
KLM said similar projects had been started in the cargo division, where it was introducing new information technology to further improve capacity utilisation.
"Enhanced joint purchasing as well as further realization of synergies with our partners are also part of Focus 2000," KLM added.
